summary: A GitHub watch and the standing observer it needs are declared in one write, so no reconcile pass can stop the observer as unused between them.

replay.detail: No replay trigger or recovery wait. The same desired claims are written; only their batching changes.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or migrations.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, registry or coordinated member upgrade change.

compatibility.detail: st gh watch on a repository without a running standing observer now writes the observer declaration and the watch subscription in one batch, under the idempotency key github-watch-observer:LOCATOR:RESOURCE+github-watch:SUBJECT:SINCE; a watch whose observer already runs keeps its earlier key. Before, the two were separate batches, and a pass between them stopped the observer as unused and the next declared it again; a member planning a watch beside that churn could be refused with stale-subject (#4831). Mixed-version fleets with the previous release interoperate: the claims are the ones that release writes and reads, a member on the previous release keeps its own two-write behaviour, and a fleet test runs a previous-release member watching beside this build's poller and checks that the poller never stops and re-declares its observer. No wire or API contract change.

downtime.detail: No storage migration or added startup work.

recovery.detail: An older build reads the combined batch like any other and goes back to two writes; nothing is stored that it cannot read.
